result.summary:
Read lib/letflow/design/iss0392-multi-task-records-collision-fix.md in full directly (not from CODE-DESIGNER's summary), plus docs/issues/ISS-0392.yaml (note: this file has no literal `acceptance_criteria:` key -- grepped and confirmed empty match -- so the '3 acceptance criteria' referenced by this handoff and by step-02-code-designer.json's own acceptance_criteria are the ones CODE-DESIGNER itself named and gated against: AC1 'no more raising on sync-completing child', AC2 'regression test scenario named precisely', AC3 'async/queued path behavior unchanged'; the design doc's own SS4 heading literally cites 'ISS-0392 AC3', confirming this is the same numbering CODE-DESIGNER worked from). Also read step-01-issue-fixer.json and step-02-code-designer.json in full for grounding.

Check-by-check verdicts (per WF-02 Step 1b, reused by WF-03 Step 2):

AC1 (no more raising on sync-completing child) -- PASS. SS2.2 defines a concrete gatekeeper TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records_once/7 with a full @spec (params, return {Ecto.Multi.t(), MapSet.t(Ecto.UUID.t())}). SS2.4 refines skip-on-repeat to replace-on-repeat with an explicit, justified ordering rule (SS2.3's dominance argument: call (2)'s snapshot strictly dominates call (1)'s because load_parent_context/2 re-reads committed state rather than reusing an in-memory value). This is a concrete, non-deferred design element directly answering the collision.

AC2 (regression test scenario named precisely) -- PASS. SS5 states the exact parent/child graph fixtures (START->HUMAN_TASK('gate')->SUB_PROCESS('sp')->END; child START->END), the exact call (Engine.complete_task/3 on the gate task), the pre-fix-must-raise assertion (exact error string/key shape) and post-fix-must-pass assertion (including a precise 'no orphan task row' content check, not just absence-of-crash), plus a second nested-cascade variant for multi-level coverage. Precise enough for TEST-DESIGNER to build directly without re-deriving the scenario.

AC3 (async/queued path unchanged) -- PASS. SS4 is a dedicated section proving the no-op sibling clause of maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/7 returns {multi, claimed_instance_ids} completely unchanged -- arity changes only, behavior is shown identical before/after, with the exact code path gating this (child_initial_state.status == :completed) named.

No TBD/deferral language on anything an AC requires resolved -- PASS. Grepped the doc for TBD/deferred/'to be determined' -- zero true hits (all 'later' occurrences are snapshot-ordering prose, not deferred work). Four open questions (SS6) reviewed individually: OQ-1 (how the MapSet crosses a Multi.merge/2 callback boundary) -- both named options already satisfy the stated contract ('exactly one step, the most recently attempted one'); this is a mechanical/idiomatic-Ecto plumbing choice, not a behavioral ambiguity affecting any AC. OQ-2 (MapSet vs list) -- stated as behaviorally identical, non-load-bearing. OQ-3 (whether the gatekeeper needs its own unit test beyond SS5's integration scenario) -- a test-coverage judgment call for TEST-DESIGNER, not an unresolved fix behavior. OQ-4 (self-referential ancestor) -- SS3's own body already commits to a specific, justified answer (replace-by-recency resolves this correctly, with the dominance argument shown to hold at every level) BEFORE OQ-4 is raised; OQ-4 only asks whether this edge case deserves its own dedicated test, not whether the design's behavior for it is determined. None of the 4 OQs leaves an AC's actual behavior undetermined.

No real .ex/.exs implementation code -- PASS. Grepped the doc for 'def '/'defp ' -- zero matches. All code-shaped blocks are fenced @spec type signatures only, no function bodies.

Function signatures fully specified (name, arity, params, return shape, error shape) -- PASS. SS2.5 and SS3 give full @spec blocks for every changed function: build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3->/4, append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6->/7, SubProcess.append_start_multi/7->/8, maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6->/7, append_completion_multi/5->/6 (success return {:ok, Multi.t()} -> {:ok, {Multi.t(), MapSet.t()}}, error return {:error, ExecutionError.error_args()} explicitly stated unchanged), build_completion_write_steps/12->/13, maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/6->/7. SS2.5's closing paragraph explicitly states no function's error return shape changes and no function gains a new failure mode.

Cross-module dependencies listed -- PASS. Design names exact call sites and signature changes across Letflow.Engine, Letflow.Engine.SubProcess, and Letflow.Engine.TaskActivation, with line-number citations for each.

VERDICT: PASS. All checks pass; no gaps to route back to CODE-DESIGNER.
